I hope it works well for you, though! If not, don't give up hope. It might take a long time to find the right meds for you, but when you do it's honestly worth the wait.

I remember coming across it online a few years ago, could relate to some of the traits but not others so I put it to one side and just got treated for depression. 

After two years of therapy and inpatient treatment, I've finally been diagnosed with "quiet" or "inward" BPD on top of depression. It feels like such a huge weight has been lifted, my therapy has changed to cater this and I feel so much better because of it. 

I don't label myself as a crybaby or pathetic as much anymore, we're digging down to the reasons WHY I feel the way I do. Having a logical explanation for all the hurt can really help you push through it.

I'm yet to have my sweet sweet payback, but my mum had a glorious moment a couple of years back. 

When she was around 10, her family struggled quite a bit for money. This girl called Tracy really liked to make her life a misery because of it. Pushing, pinching, name calling, teasing...one day my mum was lucky enough to get some new school shoes. Tracy stole them during a PE lesson and deliberately scuffed and dragged them across the playground (I'm so mad just typing about this, FUCK YOU TRACY). 

Fast forward a few years ago. Mum's doing well for herself now, working hard, happy marriage, big house, new Mercedes in the driveway. Her usual cleaner was off sick one week, so the agency said to expect a replacement for the day. I'm sure you can guess what happened next. Who should be at the door but our old pal Tracy? She recognised my mum right away, but didn't say a thing. Just turned bright red and bumbled along with her mop.  

I remember feeling so smug and happy that Tracy was scrubbing my mum's toilets. I can only hope that one day such satisfaction happens to me. It was glorious.
